exposure: Touching combined with intelligent interaction of voice and rhythm nursing mode
outcome: Quality of life scores (physiological function, psychological function, social function)
cohort: 140 newborns with feeding intolerance treated in a hospital between April 2019 and April 2021.
finding: The application of touching combined with intelligent interaction of voice and rhythm in nursing neonates with feeding intolerance significantly improved feeding performance, promoted gastrointestinal function, accelerated growth and development, shortened hospitalization, and improved quality of life compared to touch nursing alone.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference in mode of delivery between the two study groups at baseline.
